Subject: Avalon performance regression — immediate exec lifeboat

Team,

Heads up: Avalon (DL-2026-0923) is reporting sustained throughput drops and a 95th/99th tail latency spike across their production region (us-west). Error rate has increased from ~0.4% to 2.8% in the last 25 minutes. Customer-facing impact: degraded ingestion pipeline and delayed inference for high-priority traffic.

Immediate asks:
- Vivek: convene an exec lifeboat (15 min) to lock decisions (scale, fallback, credit).
- Marissa: draft a short customer update (what we know, what we’re doing, ETA).
- Aditya: start capacity provisioning and confirm reserved pool availability.

I’m starting a temp war-room (Zoom link pinned in Confluence). We need a public-facing one-paragraph status within 30 minutes and an RCA ETA within 24 hours. I’ll own customer comms unless someone objects.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

On it. Stand-up in 10 (08:30 PDT). Proposed agenda:
- Quick health snapshot (telemetry lead)
- Short-term mitigations (scale, model fallback, cache warm)
- Customer comm and credits guidance (legal & sales input)
- Rollback/canary plan if mitigation degrades QPS further

Action items I’m initiating now:
1) Request +4 reserved nodes (GPUs) in us-west — Aditya please confirm availability and ETA.
2) Trigger warm KV prefix cache for top 20 request keys to reduce cold-start cost.
3) Prepare an A/B path: route low-priority traffic to degraded but cheaper variant; keep premium traffic on primary with higher resources.

I’ll chair the lifeboat and escalate to CS/Legal if there’s an SLA breach exposure.

—Vivek

Subject: Avalon update — short customer bulletin

Bryce / Avalon team —

We understand the impact you’re seeing and are actively addressing it. Current summary:
- What happened: brief throughput regression with elevated 95th/99th latencies and a rise in error rate (~2.8%).
- What we’ve done so far: launched an executive lifeboat, requested +4 reserved nodes in us-west, warming cache prefixes for your top request patterns, preparing a model fallback for non-critical traffic.
- Next updates: a concise status bulletin in 30 minutes (08:55 PDT) and a full technical update + mitigation timeline within 3 hours.

Short-term ask from Avalon: please provide any recent config changes on your side (ingestion batch sizes, emergent spikes) — that helps narrow scope.

We’ll include a temporary traffic split and cost mitigation plan if required. I’ll work with Naomi on any formal credits/contract notes.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_fallback_plan.pdf (overview of split + fallback plan)
From: Bryce Allen <bryce@avalon.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Avalon update — short customer bulletin

Thanks for the quick response. We did not push any config changes in the last 48h; we’re seeing a spike in concurrent submits from a small partner (partner-id: PRT-774). They’re gating some traffic but that shouldn’t increase per-request compute. We’re attaching a log snippet to the ticket.

Priority for us: restore steady throughput for premium tier traffic (customer conversion flows). If a temporary route to a lower-latency variant helps, proceed. We’ll accept short-term credits if needed but need minimal manual intervention on our side — prefer Redwood-managed split.

—Bryce
Bryce Allen
Head of Platform, Avalon Systems
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Exec-Warroom <exec-warroom@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Avalon Ops <ops@avalon.com>, Bryce Allen <bryce@avalon.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Lifeboat decisions and customer-facing commitments

Summary of decisions from the 08:30 lifeboat:
- Immediate: +4 reserved nodes in us-west (Aditya confirmed; new capacity live by 08:55 PDT).
- Traffic split: 12% of low-priority traffic will be routed to the quantized variant (Q2) to relieve node pressure; premium conversion traffic stays on primary.
- Cache: KV prefix warming executed for top 20 keys (expected QPS reduction of 18%).
- Fallback plan: doc attached (proposed_fallback_plan.pdf).
- Credits posture: provisional credit up to one week of compute for verified customer impact; Sales + Legal to confirm.

Commitments to Avalon:
1) 30-minute public bulletins until stability confirmed (first done at 08:55 PDT).
2) Technical RCA draft within 24 hours; final RCA within 72 hours.
3) If we fail to meet the above, we will escalate to executive review and provide a compensatory credit proposal.

Next steps: Aditya to confirm capacity metrics once nodes are live; Marissa to publish the 08:55 bulletin; Vivek to watch telemetry and open rollback if error rate re-trends upward.

Naomi

Subject: Avalon stabilization summary & next steps

Bryce —

Status update (final for this incident window):
- Stabilization: throughput returned to baseline at ~15:40 PDT after additional capacity and the temporary traffic split. 95th/99th latencies reduced to within SLA margins. Error rate normalized to 0.5% by 15:55 PDT.
- Root cause (preliminary): a heatmap of request patterns shows an increase in a narrow keyspace (partner PRT-774) that caused an unexpected cache churn on hosts serving Avalon; combined with a late-night model parameter rollout that increased per-request memory pressure. Full RCA in 48 hours.
- Customer credits: provisional credit proposed; Sales/Legal to finalize the amount.

Attached: canary_rollout_playbook.md (detailed rollback + canary steps), slo_snapshot_0429.png (final SLO snapshot). We’ll keep this incident in postmortem rotation for follow-up items: automated hot-key detection, model rollout gating, and tighter canary thresholds.

Thanks for your partnership and patience — I’ll schedule the 48-hour RCA review with the Avalon tech leads.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
